intended_object: The left homotopy relation on edges (1-simplices) f, g : x₀ → x₁ of a (2-truncated) simplicial set: f ~ g iff there is a 2-simplex σ with d₂σ = f, d₀σ = id_{x₁} (degenerate edge) and d₁σ = g. This is the standard relation used to build the homotopy category of a quasicategory (Joyal, Lurie, Riehl). Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition is `Nonempty (CompStruct f (Edge.id x₁) g)`. A `CompStruct e₀₁ e₁₂ e₀₂` is a 2-simplex whose (0,1)-, (1,2)- and (0,2)-faces are the given edges. So `HomotopicL f g` says there is a 2-simplex with boundary (f, id, g), which is exactly the textbook left homotopy relation between edges with the same endpoints. Using `Nonempty` makes it a Prop, as the docstring says.

The generality is also right. The relation only involves 0-, 1- and 2-simplices, so a 2-truncated simplicial set is its most general natural setting. Mathlib's untruncated versions (`SSet.Edge.HomotopyL` in Quasicategory/CompStruct.lean) are defined as the same kind of structure and rely on these truncated results. No broader or competing definition of the Prop-valued relation exists in Mathlib.
